markScheme.exemplarAnswer: To calculate total resistance of a mixed network, first identify which resistors are in parallel and combine them using 1/R_total = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + …, then add any series resistances to get the overall equivalent resistance. A potential divider consists of two resistors (R1 and R2) in series across a supply voltage. The output voltage taken across R2 is V_out = V_in × R2/(R1 + R2). The voltage divides in proportion to the resistances: the larger R2 is relative to R1, the greater the output voltage. If a load is connected across R2, it forms a parallel combination with R2, reducing the effective lower resistance and therefore reducing V_out. This loading effect must be considered in practical circuits.
